doc.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Visiting studios and working at Nola Studio in New York
summary: After high school he visited studios, saw their machines, and had his first job at Nola.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So the next level after that machine that you recorded with was to go visit some recording studios?
Yeah, I used to go to all the places I could get in. I’d see the machines; the consoles were bigger and so forth.
Was this still in high school?

No this was after high school, just. There was a place in New York City called Nola Studio, and I used to see the machines they had. And I actually worked there, that was my first job, I have my social security card to prove it. It’s got Nola’s name on it to prove it. So I worked there for a while and meanwhile, also recording at home was a hobby, the whole thing was a hobby at that time.
But you were able to see what equipment they had and see what you like?
Right I learned to use it, and I used to walk for the radio store and drool when it was in the window.
